Package dev.px.core.input

Class InputService

java.lang.Object
dev.px.core.input.InputService
All Implemented Interfaces:
Named, Service
public final class InputService extends Object implements Service
Turns key and mouse events into module toggles and registered actions.

The old client did this inside a manager that also owned the GUI instances and hard-coded eight keys in an if-chain, including two that saved configs by name. Bindings are data here: a module binds through its BindSetting, and anything else registers an InputService.Action the user can rebind like any other setting.

Runs at Priority.LOW so a GUI that is capturing input can cancel the event first and stop a keystroke both typing into a text box and toggling a module.

    • capture

      public void capture(BindSetting setting)
      Routes the next key press into setting instead of acting on it.

      How a keybind button works: the GUI calls this, the user presses a key, and the binding is captured without the key also firing whatever it is currently bound to.
